newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Philips says DVD no quick fix for industry.
newsitem.headline: Philips says DVD no quick fix for industry.

text.p: An executive of Philips Electronics NV has warned that the new Digital Video Disc (DVD) format will not provide a quick fix for Europe's sluggish consumer electronics market.

Jan Oosterveld said in an interview with the Dutch news agency ANP that Philips was not rushing to launch DVD because many problems concerning the availability of software for the new format still had to be ironed out.
He said Philips would probably launch DVD players in the United States at the beginning of 1997 for $500-800 each.
DVD players would be launched somewhat later in Europe at a price of 1500-1800 guilders, he said.
DVD technology greatly increases the capacity of optical discs, allowing storage of high quality images, sound and data on one disc. One DVD disc can hold as much information as 12 CD-ROM discs.

Hardware companies from Japan, Europe and the U.S. have agreed on a single standard technology, but the film industry remains worried about home-copying and piracy despite an encryption proposal put forward by the developers of DVD.
Oosterhout said it would take time for DVD to establish itself in the market.

Philips expects some 25 million DVD players to be in use by the year 2000 -- just 10 percent of the total number of optical disc systems, the bulk of which will still be conventional compact disc (CD) players or CD-ROM drives.

"DVD is no more than an important step in the development of laser-optic systems. It is certainly not a revolutionary product like television or radio which turned the whole industry upside down," Oosterhout told ANP.
